entities.summary: John Trevisa was a Cornish writer and professional translator who played a crucial role in the transmission of classical knowledge to England during the Late Middle Ages. Born around 1320, he was educated at Oxford University and traveled extensively throughout Europe, acquiring a vast understanding of various languages and cultures. Trevisa's most notable work is his translation of Geoffrey Chaucer's 'The Canterbury Tales,' which showcased his exceptional linguistic skills and literary prowess. This achievement had significant regional implications for the development of English literature and culture, cementing Trevisa's importance as a key figure in shaping England's intellectual landscape. The impact of his translations can still be felt today, with many scholars continuing to study and appreciate his work.
